correctness.rationale: Fourier diagonalization of the globally modulated linear PDE gives exact mode amplitude exp[−(σx+κx²)t−ax∫S]. Stationary symmetric two-state Feynman–Kac has tilted eigenvalues −r±sqrt(r²+p²a²x²), with positive leading coefficient, giving Λ_p(x). Reversibly squaring its positive branch yields a²>H_p(x); direct differentiation shows H_p strictly convex with a unique minimum. Holding a>σ, change variable u=σ+κx, and the proper critical-order function has a unique minimizer satisfying 2u³−σu²−σa²=0. For a≤σ there is no positive-moment unstable mode. Discrete circle k=2πn/L gives existence iff L>L0, the exact minimum, and a near-L0 pole from n=1 only. Quadratic Taylor expansion at nondegenerate unique k* and nearest grid point yields the uniform O(L^-3) oscillatory correction and liminf/limsup. Independently evaluated σ=1, κ=0.5, r=0.7, a=1.9: p_c≈1.484251344964, x*=0.818166948817, L0≈4.683209820694, and Λ_(p_c)(x*)≈0. Finite calculations corroborate, do not prove the general asymptotics.

value.rationale: A linearly elastic surface with one spatially uniform dichotomous stochastic tension is a natural solvable alternative to spatially fluctuating active-surface models. The joint exact all-real-moment continuum/finite-circle phase diagram and a first unstable system size resolve genuinely physical and mathematical questions; geometric onset pole and universal lattice-phase oscillation are not supplied by the known single-mode telegraph exponent. The result does not predict nonlinear buckling or typical growth.

limitations: Instability is annealed p-th-moment growth, whereas every fixed mode decays almost surely.
Finite-size results apply only to one-dimensional periodic circumference L and the common global binary noise.
